A.explanation: Extension at $5.0\text{ N}$ is $3.0\text{ cm}$ and $F$ is proportional to $x$, so $x = 3.0 \times 7.0/5.0 = 4.2\text{ cm}$.

B.explanation: This value is larger than the proportional increase from $3.0\text{ cm}$ at $5.0\text{ N}$ and does not satisfy $F = kx$.

C.explanation: About $15\text{ cm}$ is the total stretched length near $7.0\text{ N}$, found from $11\text{ cm} + 4.2\text{ cm}$, not the extension.

D.explanation: This confuses spring length on the graph with extension and is much larger than the Hooke's law extension.

hints: Notice the vertical axis is spring length in $\text{cm}$, not extension: read the length at $0\text{ N}$ and at $5.0\text{ N}$.
Subtract to get the extension caused by $5.0\text{ N}$, then recall Hooke's law $F = kx$ means extension is proportional to force.
Scale that $5.0\text{ N}$ extension up to $7.0\text{ N}$ by multiplying by $7.0/5.0$, keeping the natural length of $11\text{ cm}$ separate.
walkthrough: Read the natural length from the intercept at $F = 0$: $L_0 = 11\text{ cm}$.
Read the length at $F = 5.0\text{ N}$: $L = 14\text{ cm}$, so the extension there is $x_5 = 14 - 11 = 3.0\text{ cm}$.
Hooke's law holds to $7.0\text{ N}$, so $F = kx$ with constant $k$. Hence $k = F/x_5 = 5.0/3.0\text{ N cm}^{-1}$.
This extension value, not the total length of about $15.2\text{ cm}$, is asked for. This is option A.
